raw: CHAPTER XXIII. Fire Rises
en: [Chapter 23] Fire Rises

raw: There was a change on the village where the fountain fell, and where the mender of roads went forth daily to hammer out of the stones on the highway such morsels of bread as might serve for patches to hold his poor ignorant soul and his poor reduced body together.
en: A change came over the village with the fountain, where the road-mender worked every day, breaking stones on the highway just to earn enough bread to keep his poor body and soul together. The prison on the cliff was no longer as powerful as it used to be.
ko: 도로 보수공이 형편없는 몸과 영혼을 유지할 만큼의 빵을 얻기 위해 매일 고속도로에서 돌을 깨며 일하던 분수대가 있는 마을에 변화가 찾아왔다. 절벽 위의 감옥은 예전처럼 강력하지 않았다.

raw: The prison on the crag was not so dominant as of yore; there were soldiers to guard it, but not many; there were officers to guard the soldiers, but not one of them knew what his men would do--beyond this: that it would probably not be what he was ordered.
en: There were soldiers guarding it, but not many, and there were officers to watch the soldiers. However, none of the officers knew what their men would do, except they knew the soldiers probably wouldn't obey orders.
ko: 그것을 지키는 군인들이 있었지만 많지 않았고, 군인들을 감시할 장교들도 있었다. 하지만 그 병사들이 아마도 명령에 복종하지 않을 것이라는 점 외에, 어떤 장교도 자신의 부하들이 무슨 짓을 할지 몰랐다.

raw: Far and wide lay a ruined country, yielding nothing but desolation.
en: All around, the countryside was ruined and desolate.
ko: 주변의 시골은 온통 황폐하고 적막했다.

raw: Every green leaf, every blade of grass and blade of grain, was as shrivelled and poor as the miserable people.
en: Every green leaf, blade of grass, and stalk of grain was as shriveled and poor as the miserable people themselves.
ko: 모든 푸른 잎사귀, 풀잎, 곡식 줄기는 비참한 사람들 자신만큼이나 쪼그라들고 초라했다.

raw: Everything was bowed down, dejected, oppressed, and broken.
en: Everything was beaten down, depressed, oppressed, and broken.
ko: 모든 것이 짓밟히고, 침체되고, 억압받고, 부서졌다.

raw: Habitations, fences, domesticated animals, men, women, children, and the soil that bore them--all worn out.
en: The houses, fences, farm animals, men, women, children, and even the soil they lived on were completely worn out.
ko: 집, 울타리, 가축, 남자, 여자, 아이들, 심지어 그들이 살고 있는 토양마저도 완전히 기력이 다했다.

raw: Monseigneur (often a most worthy individual gentleman) was a national blessing, gave a chivalrous tone to things, was a polite example of luxurious and shining life, and a great deal more to equal purpose; nevertheless, Monseigneur as a class had, somehow or other, brought things to this.
en: The aristocrats, who were often perfectly nice gentlemen individually, were supposed to be a blessing to the nation, setting a polite example of luxury and fine living. Yet, as a class, they had somehow brought the country to this state.
ko: 개인적으로는 종종 더할 나위 없이 좋은 신사였던 귀족들은 사치와 훌륭한 생활의 예의 바른 본보기가 되어 국가에 축복이 될 터였다. 그러나 하나의 계급으로서 그들은 어쩌다 이 나라를 이 지경으로 만들고 말았다.

raw: Strange that Creation, designed expressly for Monseigneur, should be so soon wrung dry and squeezed out!
en: It was strange that the world, which seemed to be made just for them, was so quickly squeezed dry.
ko: 오직 그들만을 위해 만들어진 것 같았던 세상이 그렇게 빨리 메말라버렸다는 것은 이상한 일이었다.

raw: There must be something short-sighted in the eternal arrangements, surely!
en: Surely, there must have been some mistake in the universe's design!
ko: 확실히, 우주의 설계에 어떤 착오가 있었음이 틀림없었다!

raw: Thus it was, however; and the last drop of blood having been extracted from the flints, and the last screw of the rack having been turned so often that its purchase crumbled, and it now turned and turned with nothing to bite, Monseigneur began to run away from a phenomenon so low and unaccountable.
en: But that was the reality. Now that the last drop of blood had been squeezed from the poorest people, and the screws of taxes and oppression could not be tightened any further without breaking, the aristocrats began to run away from this messy, confusing situation.
ko: 그러나 그것이 현실이었다. 이제 가장 가난한 사람들로부터 마지막 핏방울 하나까지 짜내고 세금과 억압의 나사가 부러지지 않고는 더 이상 조일 수 없게 되자, 귀족들은 이 엉망진창이고 혼란스러운 상황에서 도망치기 시작했다.

raw: But, this was not the change on the village, and on many a village like it.
en: But this running away was not the real change in this village, or in the many others like it.
ko: 하지만 이렇게 도망치는 것은 이 마을이나 그와 비슷한 많은 다른 마을의 진정한 변화가 아니었다.

raw: For scores of years gone by, Monseigneur had squeezed it and wrung it, and had seldom graced it with his presence except for the pleasures of the chase--now, found in hunting the people; now, found in hunting the beasts, for whose preservation Monseigneur made edifying spaces of barbarous and barren wilderness.
en: For decades, the aristocrats had squeezed the people dry, rarely visiting except to go hunting, sometimes hunting wild animals, and sometimes hunting the people themselves, keeping large areas of land wild and useless just for their sports.
ko: 수십 년 동안 귀족들은 때로는 야생 동물을 사냥하고 때로는 사람 그 자체를 사냥하러 가는 것 외에는 거의 방문하지 않은 채 사람들의 고혈을 쥐어짰으며, 오직 그들의 오락을 위해 넓은 지역의 땅을 야생 상태의 쓸모없는 곳으로 남겨 두었다.

raw: No. The change consisted in the appearance of strange faces of low caste, rather than in the disappearance of the high caste, chiselled, and otherwise beautified and beautifying features of Monseigneur.
en: No, the real change was the appearance of strange, poor-looking faces in the area, rather than the disappearance of the handsome, elegant faces of the lords.
ko: 아니다, 진정한 변화는 영주들의 잘생기고 우아한 얼굴이 사라진 것이 아니라 기이하고 초라해 보이는 얼굴들이 그 지역에 나타난 것이었다.

raw: For, in these times, as the mender of roads worked, solitary, in the dust, not often troubling himself to reflect that dust he was and to dust he must return, being for the most part too much occupied in thinking how little he had for supper and how much more he would eat if he had it--in these times, as he raised his eyes from his lonely labour, and viewed the prospect, he would see some rough figure approaching on foot, the like of which was once a rarity in those parts, but was now a frequent presence.
en: Lately, as the road-mender worked alone in the dust, not thinking about life and death, but mostly about how little he had for dinner and how much more he would eat if he could, he would look up and see a rough traveler approaching on foot. Such travelers used to be rare, but now they were a common sight. As the figure came closer, the road-mender was not surprised to see a tall, shaggy-haired man who looked almost wild.
ko: 최근에 도로 보수공은 흙먼지 속에서 홀로 일하며 삶과 죽음에 대해서는 생각하지 않고, 주로 저녁 식사가 얼마나 적은지, 할 수만 있다면 얼마나 더 먹을지에 대해 생각하다가 고개를 들어 초라한 여행자가 걸어오는 것을 보곤 했다. 그런 여행자는 드물었지만 이제는 흔한 풍경이 되었다. 그 모습이 가까워짐에 따라, 도로 보수공은 야생인처럼 보이는 털이 수북한 키 큰 남자를 보고도 놀라지 않았다.

raw: As it advanced, the mender of roads would discern without surprise, that it was a shaggy-haired man, of almost barbarian aspect, tall, in wooden shoes that were clumsy even to the eyes of a mender of roads, grim, rough, swart, steeped in the mud and dust of many highways, dank with the marshy moisture of many low grounds, sprinkled with the thorns and leaves and moss of many byways through woods.
en: The man wore wooden shoes that looked clumsy even to the road-mender. He was dirty, dark-skinned, covered in the mud and dust of many roads, damp from marshes, and covered in thorns, leaves, and moss from walking through the woods.
ko: 그 남자는 도로 보수공에게조차 투박해 보이는 나막신을 신고 있었다. 그는 더럽고 가무잡잡했으며, 수많은 도로의 진흙과 먼지로 뒤덮여 있었고 늪지대에서 와 축축했으며, 숲을 걸어오느라 가시와 나뭇잎, 이끼로 뒤덮여 있었다.

raw: Such a man came upon him, like a ghost, at noon in the July weather, as he sat on his heap of stones under a bank, taking such shelter as he could get from a shower of hail.
en: Such a man walked up to him like a ghost at noon in the hot July weather, while the road-mender sat on his pile of stones under a bank, sheltering as best he could from a sudden hailstorm.
ko: 도로 보수공이 둑 아래 돌더미에 앉아 갑작스러운 우박 폭풍을 피해 최대한 몸을 숨기고 있을 때, 뜨거운 7월 날씨의 정오에 그런 남자가 마치 유령처럼 그에게 걸어왔다.

raw: The man looked at him, looked at the village in the hollow, at the mill, and at the prison on the crag.
en: The traveler looked at him, then at the village in the valley, at the mill, and at the prison on the cliff.
ko: 여행자는 그를 본 다음, 계곡에 있는 마을, 방앗간, 절벽 위의 감옥을 바라보았다.

raw: When he had identified these objects in what benighted mind he had, he said, in a dialect that was just intelligible:
en: Once he had recognized these landmarks in his simple mind, he spoke in a rough dialect that was barely understandable:
ko: 그의 단순한 머릿속에 이 지형지물들을 알아차리자 그는 거의 알아듣기 힘든 거친 방언으로 말했다.

raw: “How goes it, Jacques?”
en: “How is it going, Jacques?”
ko: “어떻게 지내나, 자크?”

raw: “All well, Jacques.”
en: “All well, Jacques.”
ko: “모두 잘 지낸다네, 자크.”

raw: “Touch then!”
en: “Join hands then!”
ko: “그럼 손을 잡지!”

raw: They joined hands, and the man sat down on the heap of stones.
en: They shook hands, and the man sat down on the pile of stones.
ko: 그들은 악수를 나누었고, 남자는 돌더미 위에 앉았다.

raw: “No dinner?”
en: “No lunch?”
ko: “점심은 없나?”

raw: “Nothing but supper now,” said the mender of roads, with a hungry face.
en: “Nothing but dinner tonight,” said the road-mender with a hungry look.
ko: “오늘 저녁 식사 외에는 아무것도 없다네,” 도로 보수공이 굶주린 표정으로 말했다.

raw: “It is the fashion,” growled the man. “I meet no dinner anywhere.”
en: “That's the style these days,” growled the man. “I don't find lunch anywhere.”
ko: “요즘은 다들 그렇지,” 그 남자가 으르렁거렸다. “나도 어디서든 점심은 구하지 못하네.”

raw: He took out a blackened pipe, filled it, lighted it with flint and steel, pulled at it until it was in a bright glow: then, suddenly held it from him and dropped something into it from between his finger and thumb, that blazed and went out in a puff of smoke.
en: He pulled out a blackened pipe, filled it, lit it with flint and steel, and puffed until it glowed brightly. Then, he held it away and dropped a tiny pinch of something from his fingers into the bowl, which flared up and went out in a puff of smoke.
ko: 그는 새까맣게 탄 파이프를 꺼내어 채우고 부싯돌과 부시로 불을 붙인 뒤 밝게 빛날 때까지 뻐끔거렸다. 그런 다음 그는 그것을 멀리 들고 손가락으로 아주 작은 뭔가를 볼록한 통에 떨어뜨렸고, 그것은 확 타오르다 연기를 뿜으며 꺼졌다.

raw: “Touch then.” It was the turn of the mender of roads to say it this time, after observing these operations.
en: Touch hands then. It was the road mender's turn to say it this time, after watching these actions.
ko: 그럼 손을 맞대지. 이런 행동을 지켜본 후 이번에는 도로 보수공이 말할 차례였다.

raw: They again joined hands.
en: They shook hands again.
ko: 그들은 다시 악수를 했다.

raw: “To-night?” said the mender of roads.
en: “Tonight?” asked the road-mender.
ko: “오늘 밤인가?” 도로 보수공이 물었다.

raw: “To-night,” said the man, putting the pipe in his mouth.
en: “Tonight,” said the man, putting the pipe back in his mouth.
ko: “오늘 밤이지,” 남자가 파이프를 다시 입에 물며 말했다.

raw: “Where?”
en: “Where?”
ko: “어디서?”

raw: “Here.”
en: “Here.”
ko: “여기서.”

raw: He and the mender of roads sat on the heap of stones looking silently at one another, with the hail driving in between them like a pigmy charge of bayonets, until the sky began to clear over the village.
en: He and the road-mender sat on the pile of stones, staring silently at each other while the hail fell between them like a tiny army of bayonets, until the sky began to clear over the village.
ko: 그와 도로 보수공은 우박이 마치 총검으로 무장한 작은 군대처럼 그들 사이로 떨어지는 동안, 마을 위 하늘이 개기 시작할 때까지 묵묵히 서로를 바라보며 돌더미에 앉아 있었다.

raw: “Show me!” said the traveller then, moving to the brow of the hill.
en: “Show me!” said the traveler, walking to the edge of the hill.
ko: “나에게 보여주게!” 여행자가 언덕 가장자리로 걸어가며 말했다.

raw: “See!” returned the mender of roads, with extended finger. “You go down here, and straight through the street, and past the fountain--”
en: “Look!” the road-mender replied, pointing his finger. “You go down here, straight through the street, and past the fountain, ”
ko: “보시게!” 도로 보수공이 손가락으로 가리키며 대답했다. “여기서 내려가 거리를 곧장 지나 분수대를 지나면, ”

raw: “To the Devil with all that!” interrupted the other, rolling his eye over the landscape. “_I_ go through no streets and past no fountains.
en: “To the devil with all that!” the other interrupted, looking out over the landscape. “_I_ am not going through streets or past fountains.
ko: “그런 건 다 빌어먹을!” 상대방이 경치를 내다보며 말을 끊었다. “난 거리를 통과하거나 분수대를 지나갈 생각이 없어.

raw: Well?”
en: What else?”
ko: 다른 곳은?”

raw: “Well! About two leagues beyond the summit of that hill above the village.”
en: “Well, it is about six miles past the top of that hill above the village.”
ko: “글쎄, 마을 위의 저 언덕 꼭대기를 지나 6마일 정도 거리에 있다네.”

raw: “Good.
en: “Good.
ko: “좋아.

raw: When do you cease to work?”
en: When do you finish work?”
ko: 자네는 언제 일이 끝나지?”

raw: “At sunset.”
en: “At sunset.”
ko: “해 질 녘에.”

raw: “Will you wake me, before departing?
en: “Will you wake me before you leave?
ko: “떠나기 전에 나를 깨워 주겠나?

raw: I have walked two nights without resting.
en: I have walked for two nights without resting.
ko: 이틀 밤을 쉬지 않고 걸었다네.

raw: Let me finish my pipe, and I shall sleep like a child.
en: Let me finish my pipe, and I will sleep like a baby.
ko: 파이프를 다 피우고 아기처럼 자야겠어.

raw: Will you wake me?”
en: Will you wake me?”
ko: 나를 깨워 주겠지?”

raw: “Surely.”
en: “Of course.”
ko: “물론이지.”

raw: The wayfarer smoked his pipe out, put it in his breast, slipped off his great wooden shoes, and lay down on his back on the heap of stones.
en: The traveler finished smoking, put the pipe in his coat, slipped off his heavy wooden shoes, and lay down on his back on the pile of stones.
ko: 여행자는 담배를 다 피운 후 코트에 파이프를 넣고 무거운 나막신을 벗은 다음 돌더미 위에 등을 대고 누웠다.

raw: He was fast asleep directly.
en: He fell fast asleep immediately.
ko: 그는 곧바로 깊은 잠에 빠졌다.

raw: As the road-mender plied his dusty labour, and the hail-clouds, rolling away, revealed bright bars and streaks of sky which were responded to by silver gleams upon the landscape, the little man (who wore a red cap now, in place of his blue one) seemed fascinated by the figure on the heap of stones.
en: As the road-mender continued his dusty work, and the hail-clouds moved away to show bright streaks of sky that lit up the landscape with silver gleams, the little man, who now wore a red cap instead of his blue one, was fascinated by the sleeping figure.
ko: 도로 보수공이 먼지 쌓인 작업을 계속하고, 우박 구름이 물러가 은빛 섬광으로 풍경을 비추는 밝은 하늘의 줄기를 드러낼 때, 이제 파란 모자 대신 빨간 모자를 쓴 이 작은 남자는 잠자는 모습에 매료되었다.

raw: His eyes were so often turned towards it, that he used his tools mechanically, and, one would have said, to very poor account.
en: He looked at the traveler so often that he used his tools automatically and did very little actual work.
ko: 그는 여행자를 너무 자주 쳐다보아서 무의식적으로 도구를 사용할 뿐 실제 작업은 거의 하지 않았다.

raw: The bronze face, the shaggy black hair and beard, the coarse woollen red cap, the rough medley dress of home-spun stuff and hairy skins of beasts, the powerful frame attenuated by spare living, and the sullen and desperate compression of the lips in sleep, inspired the mender of roads with awe.
en: The tanned face, the shaggy black hair and beard, the coarse red wool cap, the rough mixture of homespun clothes and animal skins, the strong body thinned by starvation, and the tight, desperate look of the lips in sleep filled the road-mender with awe.
ko: 가무잡잡한 얼굴, 덥수룩한 검은 머리와 수염, 거친 붉은 털모자, 거친 홈스펀 옷과 짐승 가죽이 마구 섞인 차림새, 굶주림으로 수척해진 튼튼한 몸, 그리고 잠든 채 굳게 다문 필사적인 입술은 도로 보수공을 경외감으로 가득 채웠다.

raw: The traveller had travelled far, and his feet were footsore, and his ankles chafed and bleeding; his great shoes, stuffed with leaves and grass, had been heavy to drag over the many long leagues, and his clothes were chafed into holes, as he himself was into sores.
en: The traveler had walked a long way; his feet were sore, and his ankles were raw and bleeding. His large wooden shoes, packed with leaves and grass, must have been heavy to drag for so many miles, and his clothes were as full of holes as his body was of sores.
ko: 여행자는 먼 길을 걸어왔다. 그의 발은 욱신거렸고, 그의 발목은 벗겨져 피가 났다. 나뭇잎과 풀로 꽉 찬 큰 나막신은 그토록 많은 마일을 끌고 오기에 무거웠을 것이고, 그의 옷은 그의 몸이 상처투성이인 것만큼이나 구멍투성이였다.

raw: Stooping down beside him, the road-mender tried to get a peep at secret weapons in his breast or where not; but, in vain, for he slept with his arms crossed upon him, and set as resolutely as his lips.
en: Bending down next to him, the road-mender tried to peek at any weapons hidden in his coat, but could see nothing because the man slept with his arms crossed tightly over his chest, as firm as his closed mouth.
ko: 그의 옆에 몸을 구부린 채 도로 보수공은 그의 코트에 숨겨진 무기가 있는지 엿보려 했지만 아무것도 볼 수 없었다. 남자가 그의 다문 입만큼이나 단단하게 팔을 가슴에 꽉 꼰 채 자고 있었기 때문이다.

raw: Fortified towns with their stockades, guard-houses, gates, trenches, and drawbridges, seemed to the mender of roads, to be so much air as against this figure.
en: To the road-mender, fortified towns with their fences, guardhouses, gates, ditches, and drawbridges seemed useless against a man like this.
ko: 도로 보수공에게, 울타리, 위병소, 성문, 도랑, 도개교를 갖춘 요새화된 성읍들은 이런 남자 앞에서는 무용지물인 것처럼 보였다.

raw: And when he lifted his eyes from it to the horizon and looked around, he saw in his small fancy similar figures, stopped by no obstacle, tending to centres all over France.
en: And when he looked up from the sleeper to the horizon, he imagined thousands of similar men, stopped by no obstacles, marching toward targets all over France.
ko: 그리고 그가 잠든 사람에게서 눈을 들어 지평선을 바라보았을 때, 그는 프랑스 전역의 목표물을 향해 어떤 장애물에도 멈추지 않고 행진하는 수천 명의 비슷한 남자들을 상상했다.

raw: The man slept on, indifferent to showers of hail and intervals of brightness, to sunshine on his face and shadow, to the paltering lumps of dull ice on his body and the diamonds into which the sun changed them, until the sun was low in the west, and the sky was glowing.
en: The man slept on, ignoring the hail and the sunshine, the shadows, and the bits of ice on his body that the sun melted into glittering drops, until the sun was low in the west and the sky was glowing.
ko: 그 남자는 해가 서쪽으로 기울고 하늘이 붉게 타오를 때까지 우박과 햇살, 그림자, 햇빛에 녹아 반짝이는 물방울로 변한 몸의 얼음조각들을 무시한 채 계속 잠을 잤다.

raw: Then, the mender of roads having got his tools together and all things ready to go down into the village, roused him.
en: Then, the road-mender gathered his tools, got ready to go down to the village, and woke him up.
ko: 그런 다음, 도로 보수공은 자신의 도구를 챙기고 마을로 내려갈 준비를 하며 그를 깨웠다.

raw: “Good!” said the sleeper, rising on his elbow. “Two leagues beyond the summit of the hill?”
en: “Good!” said the sleeper, sitting up on his elbow. “About six miles past the top of the hill?”
ko: “좋아!” 잠자던 남자가 팔꿈치를 괴고 일어나 앉으며 말했다. “언덕 꼭대기를 지나서 약 6마일이었지?”

raw: “About.”
en: “About that.”
ko: “그 정도 될 거야.”

raw: “About.
en: “About that.
ko: “그것에 관하여.”

raw: Good!”
en: Good!”
ko: “좋아!”

raw: The mender of roads went home, with the dust going on before him according to the set of the wind, and was soon at the fountain, squeezing himself in among the lean kine brought there to drink, and appearing even to whisper to them in his whispering to all the village.
en: The road-mender walked home, the wind blowing the dust ahead of him. Soon he was at the fountain, squeezing in among the thin cattle brought there to drink, looking as if he were whispering to them just as he was whispering to the rest of the village.
ko: 도로 보수공은 바람이 그의 앞의 먼지를 날리는 가운데 집으로 걸어갔다. 곧 그는 분수대에 도착했고, 마실 것을 찾아 그곳으로 온 마른 소들 사이에 끼어들어, 마치 그가 마을 사람들에게 속삭였던 것처럼 소들에게도 속삭이는 듯한 표정을 지었다.

raw: When the village had taken its poor supper, it did not creep to bed, as it usually did, but came out of doors again, and remained there.
en: Once the villagers had eaten their poor dinner, they did not go to bed as they usually did, but came back outside and stayed there.
ko: 마을 사람들은 빈약한 저녁 식사를 마친 후, 평소처럼 잠자리에 들지 않고 밖으로 나와 그곳에 머물렀다.

raw: A curious contagion of whispering was upon it, and also, when it gathered together at the fountain in the dark, another curious contagion of looking expectantly at the sky in one direction only.
en: A strange epidemic of whispering spread among them, and as they gathered in the dark around the fountain, another strange urge made them all look at the sky in the same direction.
ko: 기이한 속삭임의 전염병이 그들 사이에 퍼졌고, 어둠 속에서 분수대 주변에 모여들자 또 다른 이상한 충동으로 인해 모두가 같은 방향의 하늘을 바라보게 되었다.

raw: Monsieur Gabelle, chief functionary of the place, became uneasy; went out on his house-top alone, and looked in that direction too; glanced down from behind his chimneys at the darkening faces by the fountain below, and sent word to the sacristan who kept the keys of the church, that there might be need to ring the tocsin by-and-bye.
en: Monsieur Gabelle, the local official, became nervous. He went out on his rooftop alone and looked in that direction too. He peered down from behind his chimneys at the gloomy faces around the fountain below, and sent a message to the church official who had the keys, telling him they might need to ring the alarm bell soon.
ko: 지역 관리인 가벨 씨는 초조해졌다. 그도 혼자 지붕 위로 올라가 그 방향을 바라보았다. 그는 굴뚝 뒤에서 아래 분수대 주변의 우울한 얼굴들을 내려다보며, 열쇠를 가진 교회 관리인에게 메시지를 보내 곧 경보종을 울려야 할지도 모른다고 전했다.

raw: The night deepened.
en: The night grew darker.
ko: 밤은 더욱 어두워졌다.

raw: The trees environing the old chateau, keeping its solitary state apart, moved in a rising wind, as though they threatened the pile of building massive and dark in the gloom.
en: The trees surrounding the old chateau, which stood isolated and grand, swayed in a rising wind as if threatening the massive, dark building.
ko: 고립되고 웅장하게 서 있는 낡은 성을 둘러싼 나무들은 마치 거대하고 어두운 건물을 위협하듯 거세지는 바람에 흔들렸다.

raw: Up the two terrace flights of steps the rain ran wildly, and beat at the great door, like a swift messenger rousing those within; uneasy rushes of wind went through the hall, among the old spears and knives, and passed lamenting up the stairs, and shook the curtains of the bed where the last Marquis had slept.
en: Rain poured down the two stone terraces and beat against the great door like a messenger trying to wake the people inside. Drafts of wind blew through the hall, rattling the old spears and knives, and swept up the stairs, shaking the curtains of the bed where the late Marquis used to sleep.
ko: 비가 두 개의 돌 테라스로 쏟아져 내렸고, 마치 안의 사람들을 깨우려는 전령처럼 거대한 문을 두드렸다. 바람이 현관을 뚫고 불어와 낡은 창과 칼들을 덜그럭거리게 했고, 계단을 휩쓸고 올라가 고인이 된 후작이 자던 침대의 커튼을 흔들었다.

raw: East, West, North, and South, through the woods, four heavy-treading, unkempt figures crushed the high grass and cracked the branches, striding on cautiously to come together in the courtyard.
en: From the East, West, North, and South, through the woods, four rough, messy figures stepped heavily through the high grass and snapped branches, walking cautiously to meet in the courtyard.
ko: 숲을 지나 동, 서, 남, 북에서 네 명의 거칠고 지저분한 인물들이 높은 풀을 헤치고 나뭇가지를 꺾으며 무거운 발걸음으로 조심스럽게 안뜰로 모여들었다.

raw: Four lights broke out there, and moved away in different directions, and all was black again.
en: Four lights suddenly appeared there, moved off in different directions, and then everything went dark again.
ko: 그곳에서 갑자기 네 개의 불빛이 나타났다가 서로 다른 방향으로 멀어졌고, 그러고 나서 모든 것이 다시 어두워졌다.

raw: But, not for long.
en: But not for long.
ko: 하지만 그리 오래가지는 않았다.

raw: Presently, the chateau began to make itself strangely visible by some light of its own, as though it were growing luminous.
en: Soon, the chateau began to glow with a strange light of its own.
ko: 머지않아 성은 그 자체의 이상한 빛으로 번쩍이기 시작했다.

raw: Then, a flickering streak played behind the architecture of the front, picking out transparent places, and showing where balustrades, arches, and windows were.
en: A flickering flame danced behind the front of the building, lighting up the arches, balconies, and windows from within.
ko: 건물 정면 뒤로 깜박이는 불꽃이 춤을 추며 아치, 발코니, 그리고 안쪽의 창문들을 환하게 밝혔다.

raw: Then it soared higher, and grew broader and brighter.
en: Then the fire rose higher, growing wider and brighter.
ko: 그러자 불길이 더 높이 솟아오르며 더 넓고 더 밝아졌다.

raw: Soon, from a score of the great windows, flames burst forth, and the stone faces awakened, stared out of fire.
en: Soon, flames burst out of twenty large windows, and the stone faces carved on the walls seemed to wake up and stare out from the fire.
ko: 곧 스무 개의 커다란 창문에서 불꽃이 뿜어져 나왔고, 벽에 새겨진 돌 얼굴들이 잠에서 깨어나 불길 속에서 밖을 내다보는 듯했다.

raw: A faint murmur arose about the house from the few people who were left there, and there was a saddling of a horse and riding away.
en: A quiet panic arose inside the house among the few servants left behind. A horse was quickly saddled, and someone rode away.
ko: 남겨진 소수의 하인들 사이에서 집 안에서는 조용한 패닉이 일어났다. 재빨리 말에 안장을 얹었고, 누군가가 말을 타고 떠났다.

raw: There was spurring and splashing through the darkness, and bridle was drawn in the space by the village fountain, and the horse in a foam stood at Monsieur Gabelle’s door. “Help, Gabelle!
en: Spurring the horse through the dark, splashing in the mud, the rider stopped at the village fountain, the sweating horse panting at Monsieur Gabelle's door. “Help, Gabelle!
ko: 진흙탕을 튀기며 어둠 속을 달려, 땀에 흠뻑 젖어 헐떡이는 말이 가벨 씨의 문 앞 분수대에 멈춰 섰다. “도와줘요, 가벨!

raw: Help, every one!” The tocsin rang impatiently, but other help (if that were any) there was none.
en: Help, everyone!” The church alarm bell began to ring urgently, but no help came.
ko: 모두 도와줘요!” 교회의 경보종이 다급하게 울리기 시작했지만, 아무런 도움도 오지 않았다.

raw: The mender of roads, and two hundred and fifty particular friends, stood with folded arms at the fountain, looking at the pillar of fire in the sky. “It must be forty feet high,” said they, grimly; and never moved.
en: The road-mender and two hundred and fifty of his fellow villagers stood by the fountain with their arms crossed, watching the pillar of fire in the sky. “It must be forty feet high,” they said grimly, and none of them moved a muscle to help.
ko: 도로 보수공과 이백오십 명의 마을 사람들은 분수대 곁에 팔짱을 끼고 서서 하늘로 솟구치는 불기둥을 바라보았다. 그들은 “아마 높이가 사십 피트는 될 거야”라고 무뚝뚝하게 말했고, 그들 중 누구도 돕기 위해 움직이지 않았다.

raw: The rider from the chateau, and the horse in a foam, clattered away through the village, and galloped up the stony steep, to the prison on the crag.
en: The rider from the chateau, on his sweating horse, clattered out of the village and galloped up the rocky path to the prison on the cliff.
ko: 땀 흘리는 말을 탄 성에서 온 기사는 마을 밖으로 요란하게 달려 절벽 위의 감옥으로 이어지는 바위 길을 뛰어올랐다.

raw: At the gate, a group of officers were looking at the fire; removed from them, a group of soldiers. “Help, gentlemen--officers!
en: At the gate, a group of officers stood watching the fire, and a little distance away, a group of soldiers watched too. “Help, officers!
ko: 성문에는 한 무리의 장교들이 서서 불을 지켜보고 있었고, 조금 떨어진 곳에서는 군인들도 지켜보고 있었다. “도와주십시오, 장교님들!

raw: The chateau is on fire; valuable objects may be saved from the flames by timely aid!
en: The chateau is on fire! We can save valuable things if we act now!
ko: 성에 불이 났습니다! 지금 행동하면 귀중품들을 구할 수 있습니다!

raw: Help, help!” The officers looked towards the soldiers who looked at the fire; gave no orders; and answered, with shrugs and biting of lips, “It must burn.”
en: Help!” The officers looked at the soldiers, who just stared at the fire. The officers gave no orders and, shrugging their shoulders and biting their lips, replied, “It must burn.”
ko: 도와주십시오!” 장교들은 불을 멍하니 쳐다보고만 있는 군인들을 바라보았다. 장교들은 아무런 명령도 내리지 않았고, 어깨를 으쓱하고 입술을 깨물며 “타버려야지”라고 대답했다.

raw: As the rider rattled down the hill again and through the street, the village was illuminating.
en: As the rider rode back down the hill and through the street, the village was lighting up in celebration.
ko: 기사가 다시 언덕을 내려와 거리를 지날 때, 마을은 축하 분위기로 환하게 빛나고 있었다.

raw: The mender of roads, and the two hundred and fifty particular friends, inspired as one man and woman by the idea of lighting up, had darted into their houses, and were putting candles in every dull little pane of glass.
en: The road-mender and his two hundred and fifty friends, all sharing the same idea, had run into their houses to put candles in every small window pane.
ko: 도로 보수공과 그의 이백오십 명의 친구들은 모두 같은 생각을 공유하며 집 안으로 뛰어들어가 모든 작은 유리창에 촛불을 놓았다.

raw: The general scarcity of everything, occasioned candles to be borrowed in a rather peremptory manner of Monsieur Gabelle; and in a moment of reluctance and hesitation on that functionary’s part, the mender of roads, once so submissive to authority, had remarked that carriages were good to make bonfires with, and that post-horses would roast.
en: Because candles were scarce like everything else, they demanded to borrow them from Monsieur Gabelle. When the official hesitated to give them up, the road-mender, who had once been so obedient, remarked that carriages made great bonfires and carriage-horses would roast nicely.
ko: 다른 모든 것들처럼 양초도 부족했기 때문에, 그들은 가벨 씨에게 그것을 빌려달라고 요구했다. 그 관리가 내어주기를 망설이자, 한때 아주 순종적이었던 도로 보수공은 마차들이 훌륭한 모닥불이 될 것이고 마차를 끄는 말들은 맛있게 구워질 것이라고 한마디 했다.

raw: The chateau was left to itself to flame and burn.
en: The chateau was left alone to burn.
ko: 성은 홀로 불타도록 버려졌다.

raw: In the roaring and raging of the conflagration, a red-hot wind, driving straight from the infernal regions, seemed to be blowing the edifice away.
en: In the roaring heat of the fire, a scorching wind, looking as if it blew straight from hell, seemed to tear at the building.
ko: 맹렬한 불의 열기 속에서, 마치 지옥에서 곧장 불어오는 듯한 찌는 듯한 바람이 건물을 찢어놓는 듯했다.

raw: With the rising and falling of the blaze, the stone faces showed as if they were in torment.
en: As the flames flickered, the stone faces carved on the walls looked as if they were crying out in pain.
ko: 불꽃이 깜박일 때, 벽에 조각된 돌 얼굴들은 마치 고통에 비명을 지르는 것처럼 보였다.

raw: When great masses of stone and timber fell, the face with the two dints in the nose became obscured: anon struggled out of the smoke again, as if it were the face of the cruel Marquis, burning at the stake and contending with the fire.
en: When huge chunks of stone and wood fell, the face with the two dents in the nose was hidden for a moment, then peeked out of the smoke again, looking like the face of the cruel Marquis himself, burning at the stake and fighting the fire.
ko: 돌과 나무의 거대한 조각들이 떨어질 때, 코에 두 개의 흠집이 있는 얼굴이 잠시 가려졌다가 연기 속에서 다시 나타났는데, 마치 잔인한 후작 자신의 얼굴이 화형대에서 불타며 불길과 싸우는 듯했다.

raw: The chateau burned; the nearest trees, laid hold of by the fire, scorched and shrivelled; trees at a distance, fired by the four fierce figures, begirt the blazing edifice with a new forest of smoke.
en: The chateau burned. The nearest trees caught fire and shriveled up, while trees further away, set on fire by the four mysterious men, surrounded the burning building with a thick forest of smoke.
ko: 성이 불탔다. 가장 가까운 나무들에 불이 붙어 시들어버렸고, 더 멀리 있는 나무들은 네 명의 신비로운 남자들이 불을 질러 두꺼운 연기의 숲으로 불타는 건물을 둘러쌌다.

raw: Molten lead and iron boiled in the marble basin of the fountain; the water ran dry; the extinguisher tops of the towers vanished like ice before the heat, and trickled down into four rugged wells of flame.
en: Melted lead and iron bubbled in the marble fountain basin. The water dried up completely. The pointed roofs of the towers melted like ice in the heat, dripping down into four fiery pits.
ko: 녹은 납과 철이 대리석 분수대 그릇 안에서 부글부글 끓었다. 물은 완전히 말라버렸다. 탑의 뾰족한 지붕들은 열기에 얼음처럼 녹아내려 네 개의 불타는 구덩이 속으로 뚝뚝 떨어졌다.

raw: Great rents and splits branched out in the solid walls, like crystallisation; stupefied birds wheeled about and dropped into the furnace; four fierce figures trudged away, East, West, North, and South, along the night-enshrouded roads, guided by the beacon they had lighted, towards their next destination.
en: Giant cracks split the solid walls, birds flew in confused circles before falling into the heat, and the four fierce men walked away to the East, West, North, and South along the dark roads, guided by the massive light they had created.
ko: 거대한 균열이 단단한 벽을 쪼개었고, 새들은 열기 속으로 떨어지기 전에 혼란스럽게 빙빙 돌며 날아다녔으며, 네 명의 사나운 남자들은 그들이 만들어낸 거대한 빛의 인도를 받으며 어두운 길을 따라 동, 서, 남, 북으로 걸어갔다.

raw: The illuminated village had seized hold of the tocsin, and, abolishing the lawful ringer, rang for joy.
en: In the lit-up village, the people took over the church bell, kicked out the official bell-ringer, and rang the bell in celebration.
ko: 환하게 밝혀진 마을에서 사람들은 교회 종을 차지하고, 공식 종지기를 쫓아낸 뒤 축하하며 종을 울렸다.

raw: Not only that; but the village, light-headed with famine, fire, and bell-ringing, and bethinking itself that Monsieur Gabelle had to do with the collection of rent and taxes--though it was but a small instalment of taxes, and no rent at all, that Gabelle had got in those latter days--became impatient for an interview with him, and, surrounding his house, summoned him to come forth for personal conference.
en: Not only that, but the villagers, dizzy from hunger, excitement, and bell-ringing, remembered that Monsieur Gabelle was the one who collected rents and taxes, even though he had collected very little lately. They wanted to speak with him, so they surrounded his house and shouted for him to come out.
ko: 그뿐만 아니라, 굶주림과 흥분, 그리고 종치기로 어지러워진 마을 사람들은 최근 들어 아주 적게 징수하긴 했지만, 가벨 씨가 임대료와 세금을 징수하는 사람이었다는 사실을 기억해냈다. 그들은 그와 이야기하고 싶어서 그의 집을 에워싸고 밖으로 나오라고 소리쳤다.

raw: Whereupon, Monsieur Gabelle did heavily bar his door, and retire to hold counsel with himself.
en: Monsieur Gabelle quickly locked and barred his doors and sat down to think about what to do.
ko: 가벨 씨는 재빨리 문을 잠그고 빗장을 지른 후, 어떻게 해야 할지 생각하며 주저앉았다.

raw: The result of that conference was, that Gabelle again withdrew himself to his housetop behind his stack of chimneys; this time resolved, if his door were broken in (he was a small Southern man of retaliative temperament), to pitch himself head foremost over the parapet, and crush a man or two below.
en: His decision was to climb back onto his roof behind the chimneys. He resolved that if the crowd broke down his door, he, being a small man from the south of France with a stubborn streak, would throw himself off the roof to crush one or two of them on his way down.
ko: 그의 결정은 굴뚝 뒤의 지붕 위로 다시 기어 올라가는 것이었다. 그는 군중이 문을 부수고 들어온다면, 프랑스 남부 출신의 체구가 작고 고집이 센 자신이 지붕에서 몸을 던져 떨어지는 길에 그들 중 한두 명을 깔아뭉개겠다고 결심했다.

raw: Probably, Monsieur Gabelle passed a long night up there, with the distant chateau for fire and candle, and the beating at his door, combined with the joy-ringing, for music; not to mention his having an ill-omened lamp slung across the road before his posting-house gate, which the village showed a lively inclination to displace in his favour.
en: Monsieur Gabelle spent a very long night up there, using the burning chateau in the distance as his light, and the pounding on his door and the joyous bell-ringing as his music. Outside his gate, a street lantern hung across the road, and the villagers were dropping hints that they would love to hang him from it.
ko: 가벨 씨는 멀리서 불타는 성을 불빛 삼아, 그의 문을 두드리는 소리와 기쁨에 찬 종소리를 음악 삼아 그곳에서 아주 긴 밤을 보냈다. 그의 문 밖 도로에는 가로등이 매달려 있었고, 마을 사람들은 그를 거기에 매달고 싶다는 힌트를 흘리고 있었다.

raw: A trying suspense, to be passing a whole summer night on the brink of the black ocean, ready to take that plunge into it upon which Monsieur Gabelle had resolved!
en: It was a terrifying way to spend a summer night, standing on the edge of death, ready to jump if he had to.
ko: 어쩔 수 없다면 뛰어내릴 준비를 한 채 죽음의 가장자리에 서서 여름밤을 보내는 것은 끔찍한 일이었다.

raw: But, the friendly dawn appearing at last, and the rush-candles of the village guttering out, the people happily dispersed, and Monsieur Gabelle came down bringing his life with him for that while.
en: But when morning finally came and the villagers' candles burned out, the crowd dispersed, and Monsieur Gabelle was able to climb down, safe for the moment.
ko: 하지만 마침내 아침이 밝아오고 마을 사람들의 촛불이 다 타버리자, 군중은 흩어졌고 가벨 씨는 당분간은 안전하게 내려올 수 있었다.

raw: Within a hundred miles, and in the light of other fires, there were other functionaries less fortunate, that night and other nights, whom the rising sun found hanging across once-peaceful streets, where they had been born and bred; also, there were other villagers and townspeople less fortunate than the mender of roads and his fellows, upon whom the functionaries and soldiery turned with success, and whom they strung up in their turn.
en: Within a hundred miles, by the light of other fires, other officials were not as lucky. That night and over the next few nights, the morning sun found many of them hanging dead over the streets where they had grown up. On the other side, some villagers were less fortunate than the road-mender and his friends, as soldiers and officials caught them and hanged them instead.
ko: 백 마일 이내의 다른 관리들은 다른 불빛 아래에서 그렇게 운이 좋지 않았다. 그날 밤과 이어진 며칠 밤 동안, 아침 해는 그들 중 많은 이들이 그들이 자란 거리 위에서 목매달려 죽어 있는 것을 발견했다. 반대편에서는 군인들과 관리들이 마을 사람들을 붙잡아 대신 교수형에 처했기 때문에, 도로 보수공과 그의 친구들보다 운이 나쁜 마을 사람들도 있었다.

raw: But, the fierce figures were steadily wending East, West, North, and South, be that as it would; and whosoever hung, fire burned.
en: But the mysterious men continued their march to the East, West, North, and South.
ko: 그러나 신비로운 남자들은 동, 서, 남, 북으로 그들의 행진을 계속했다.

raw: The altitude of the gallows that would turn to water and quench it, no functionary, by any stretch of mathematics, was able to calculate successfully.
en: No matter who was hanged, the fires of rebellion kept burning, and no official could figure out how to put them out.
ko: 누가 교수형을 당하든 반란의 불길은 계속 타올랐고, 어떤 관리도 그것을 끌 방법을 알아내지 못했다.
